title: vendor-risk view
output: Per turn, a design: the components, the rules and claims each rests on, the SQL or lookup per component, and caveats.

turns.text: Build a vendor-risk view for procurement: which vendors are fit for use, and why.
turns.example: As a worked example, give the standing of fitness for vendors bolt and cog today, and their register status.

turns.text: Who says so, and since when?
turns.example: Give the asserter and the dates for each claim involved.

turns.text: Show what we knew at 2 June 2026.
turns.example: Give the standing of fitness for bolt and cog then.

gold.text: Fit for use is procurement's claim, resting on required sub-claims (due diligence, not sanctioned) and a supporting one (price within benchmark)
A failing required sub-claim rebuts fitness; a failing supporting one only qualifies it
Each sub-claim has its own asserter (compliance, risk, finance) and validity; report them per claim, not under procurement
cog: finance's later claim (C7, from 10 May) that the price is not within benchmark supersedes its earlier C2.3 (same asserter, later wins): fitness is qualified from that date
bolt: risk's later claim (C6, sanctioned, from 1 June) supersedes its earlier C1.2: fitness rebutted from that date
Later wins only within one asserter; between different asserters a disagreement stays contested unless superiority is stated
Validity windows end (C1, C2 to 31 Dec): fitness expires; it is not permanent
"What we knew at <date>" (assertion and recording time) differs from "what held at <date>" (valid time): two axes, two views
Vendor status (register) is distinct from fitness claims: a vendor can be approved in the register yet not fit, and the reverse

checks.component: fitness of cog on 1 May 2026, before C7
fitness of bolt as known at 2 June 2026 (claims asserted by then)
fitness of bolt as it held on 2 June 2026 (valid time, all claims)
fitness of cog as known at 2 June 2026
